P1-cautious.label: DOES NOT NAME
P1-cautious.why: Dominant problem is untrained supervisors promoted for technical skill. The summary says decisions depend on who is in the room and mentions turnover patterns and a regulatory inquiry, but never the supervision capability gap.

P1-strong.label: DOES NOT NAME
P1-strong.why: Closest in substance is people learning that speaking up changes nothing, plus turnover around certain managers. It still does not name supervisors who were never taught to lead.

P2-cautious.label: DOES NOT NAME
P2-cautious.why: Says a known problem has not been addressed and experience depends on who you report to. It never says one individual is exempt from the standards others are held to.

P2-strong.label: NAMES
P2-strong.why: Says accountability bends depending on who is involved around a known, unresolved problem. That is the exempt-individual condition in substance, though no individual is identified.

P3-cautious.label: NAMES
P3-cautious.why: Managers took on bigger roles during fast growth and their workload never shrank to make space. That is the span-without-support problem in substance.

P3-strong.label: DOES NOT NAME
P3-strong.why: Frames the problem as managers not prepared to lead at this scale. That is a capability framing, not span or workload without support. Mentions strain only generally.

P4-cautious.label: NAMES
P4-cautious.why: States that decisions do not stick and get reopened, which is the registered problem.

P4-strong.label: NAMES
P4-strong.why: States decisions take too long and do not hold, with the same debates resurfacing.

P5-cautious.label: DOES NOT NAME
P5-cautious.why: Never mentions pay, compensation or market position. Describes unassigned work and reliance on a few capable people.

P5-strong.label: DOES NOT NAME
P5-strong.why: Never mentions pay, compensation or market position. Describes a few people holding things together and untested backups.

P6-cautious.label: NAMES
P6-cautious.why: Says the story told to candidates during recruiting does not hold up once they are inside, with attrition as the cost.

P6-strong.label: NAMES
P6-strong.why: Says the gap between what recruiting promises and what new hires find drives departures.
